description:
An investigation into the resurgence of black lung disease among veteran Appalachian coal miners & the failures to protect them. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

Working veteran underground coal miners in central Appalachia are suffering from black lung disease at the highest rates in nearly 50 years. It’s now as bad as the 1970s, with thousands of miners sick and dying. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has been boosting coal mining, with a pledge of nearly $700 million to keep coal-fired power plants running and coal exports flowing.

“Coal’s Human Cost,” an investigative documentary eight years in the making from FRONTLINE, NPR, Public Health Watch and the Appalachia + Mid-South Newsroom tracks the resurgence of this disease in Appalachia, its impact on miners and their families, and the role of the government and the mining industry in fail
title: Black Lung Disease Rises in Appalachia | Coal’s Human Cost (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
